title: Logarithmic singularity in a dynamical quantum phase transition for free fermions
authors: Yasser Bezzaz, Dimitri M. Gangardt, Pavel L. Krapivsky, Jean-Marc Luck, Kirone Mallick, Sylvain Prolhac
abstract: We study the Loschmidt echo in a system of N non-interacting spinless lattice fermions released from a double-domain-wall initial state. In the large-N limit, the return probability is characterized by a large-deviation rate function known as the dynamical free energy. The Loschmidt echo is dominated by a complex instanton configuration, and the dynamical free energy develops a logarithmic singularity at the dynamical quantum phase transition. We obtain analytical results in the short-time and long-time regimes and support them with numerical computations. We show that the transition can be understood as a topological change of the dominant instanton configuration, analogous to the emergence of a cut in random matrix theory. We further show that post-selection can drive the system through two successive DQPTs, associated with successive topological changes of the dominant instanton configuration in complex time.
summary: This work analyzes the Loschmidt echo for free fermions undergoing a dynamical quantum phase transition (DQPT). By mapping the problem to instanton calculations, the authors show that the transition manifests as a logarithmic singularity in the dynamical free energy. This provides a deep connection between quantum quench dynamics, topology, and large-deviation theory.
main_problem: The paper investigates the Loschmidt echo in a system undergoing a dynamical quantum phase transition (DQPT).
main_result: The dynamical free energy develops a logarithmic singularity at the DQPT, which is understood as a topological change in the dominant instanton configuration.
method: The analysis uses large-deviation theory, mapping the problem to a Coulomb gas model and employing instanton calculations in the complex time plane.
model_or_system: The system consists of N non-interacting spinless lattice fermions on a 1D lattice, initialized in a double-domain-wall state. The dynamics are governed by a tight-binding Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Loschmidt echo, dynamical free energy, and the instanton configuration.
important_parameters: Large N limit, large time limit, and the rescaled time $\tau = t/N$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-N limit and the characterization of the echo by the dominant complex instanton configuration.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the initial double-domain-wall configuration and the topological change of the dominant instanton configuration across the critical point.
paper_structure: The paper reviews known results, maps the problem to the Coulomb gas, analyzes the real-time DQPT, and extends the analysis to complex time to study post-selection effects.
why_interesting: The connection between non-equilibrium quantum dynamics (Loschmidt echo) and topological phase transitions, using tools from random matrix theory and large deviations, is highly relevant to understanding quantum thermalization and non-equilibrium critical phenomena.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Topological change of the dominant instanton configuration across the critical rescaled time τ = τc in the complex plane z = eiq. Red dots show the discrete saddle points from solving numerically (21) for N = 90. The curves in black represent the density support of the saddle points in the continuous limit by solving (29).

Figure 3: Phase diagram of the dominant instanton configuration for AN(τ) in the complex plane of τ. Typical shapes of the charge support are shown in each region. The point of merger of the two critical lines for τ = i/2 corresponds to the third- order Gross-Witten-Wadia transition.

Figure 4: Order parameter c(τ). The colored curves are extracted from the finite- N Loschmidt amplitude computed through the Toeplitz determinant representa- tion (15). The black dashed curve is the large-N solution obtained from Eq. (45). The open circles indicate the exact short-time result c(τ) = −4τ2, while the grey dotted line denotes the large-time asymptote c(∞) = −1/2. The inset highlights the convergence of the finite-N results near the critical point.

Figure 5: Evolution of the dominant instanton configuration in the short-time regime in the complex plane z = eiq. From left to right: τ = 0.25, τ = 0.29, and τ ≃τc = 0.331, with N = 40, N = 90, and N = 90, respectively. Red dots show the discrete saddle points obtained by solving numerically (21), while the black curve represents the continuum support γ determined exactly in (53). Black dots indicate the zeros of y(z), and the grey dotted curve is the unit circle. As τ approaches τc, the zeros move toward the support, which continuously deforms into the unbroken- heart configuration at the transition.

Figure 6: Evolution of the dominant instanton configuration in the long-time regime. From left to right: τ = 0.5, τ = 1, and τ = 10, with N = 90. Red dots show the discrete saddle points obtained by solving numerically (21), while the black curves represent the continuum support γ determined from (29). Black dots indicate the branch points of y(z) and the endpoints of the support. The grey dotted curve is the unit circle. In this regime, the support consists of two symmetric disconnected cuts forming the broken-heart configuration. As τ increases, the two cuts continuously approach the steepest-descent contours of the external potential.
